# Job Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 416v–417r

---

**3:1** After this Iyyov opened [patach] his-mouth and-cursed [vayeqallel] his-day [yomo].

**3:2** And-answered [vaya'an] Iyyov and-said:

**3:3** "Let-perish [yovad] the-day I-was-born in-it [ivvaled bo],
and-the-night [it] said, 'A-man-child [gever] is-conceived [horah].'

**3:4** The-day that — let-it-be darkness [choshekh];
let-not God [eloah] seek-it [yidreshehu] from-above [mi-ma'al],
and-let-not shine [tofiya] upon-it light [neharah].

**3:5** Let-redeem-it [yig'aluhu] darkness [choshekh] and-deep-shadow [tsalmaveth];
let-dwell upon-it a-cloud [ananah];
let-terrify-it [yevatuhu] the-blacknesses of-the-day [kimrirei yom].

**3:6** The-night that — let-thick-darkness [ofel] seize-it [yiqqachehu];
let-it-not rejoice [yichad] among-the-days of-the-year;
into-the-number of-the-months let-it-not come [yavo].

**3:7** Behold, the-night that — let-it-be barren [galmud];
let-no joyful-cry [renanah] come in-it.

**3:8** Let-curse-it [yiqqevuhu] the-cursers of-the-day [orerey yom],
those-ready [ha-atidim] to-rouse [orer] Leviathan [livyatan].

**3:9** Let-be-dark [yechsheku] the-stars of-its-twilight [nishpo];
let-it-wait [yeqav] for-light and-there-be-none [ve-ayin],
and-let-it-not see [yir'eh] the-eyelids of-the-dawn [af'appei shachar].

**3:10** For it-did-not shut [sagar] the-doors of-my-womb [bitni],
and-did-not hide [yaster] trouble [amal] from-my-eyes.

**3:11** Why did-I-not from-the-womb [me-rechem] die [amut]?
From-the-belly [mi-beten] I-came-out and-expired [egva]?

**3:12** Why did-knees [birkayim] receive-me [qiddemuniy],
and-why breasts [shadayim] that I-should-suck [inaq]?

**3:13** For now I-would-have-lain-down [shakhavti] and-been-quiet [eshqot];
I-would-have-slept [yashaneti] — then rest [menucha] to-me.

**3:14** With-kings and-counselors [yoatsei] of-the-earth [arets],
who-built [bonim] ruins [choravot] for-themselves;

**3:15** Or with-princes [sarim] who-had gold [zahav],
who-filled [memaleim] their-houses [batteihem] with-silver [kesef].

**3:16** Or like-a-miscarriage [nefel] hidden [tamun] I-would-not be,
like-infants [olelim] who-did-not see light [or].

**3:17** There the-wicked [resha'im] cease [chadelu] raging [rogez],
and-there the-weary of-strength [yegi'ei koach] rest [yanuchu].

**3:18** Together prisoners [asirim] are-at-ease [sha'ananu];
they-do-not hear the-voice of-the-taskmaster [noges].

**3:19** Small [qaton] and-great [gadol] — there he [is],
and-a-servant [eved] free [chofshi] from-his-master.

**3:20** Why does-he-give [yitten] to-the-weary [la-amel] light [or],
and-life [chayyim] to-the-bitter of-soul [le-marei nefesh]?

**3:21** The-ones-waiting [ha-mechakim] for-death [la-mavet] and-it-is-not [ve-eynenu],
and-they-dig-for-it [yachperuhu] more-than-for-hidden-treasures [mi-matmonim].

**3:22** The-ones-rejoicing [ha-semechim] unto exultation [elei gilo],
they-are-glad [yasisu] when they-find [yimtse'u] a-grave [qaver].

**3:23** To-a-man [le-gever] whose-way [darkho] is-hidden [nisterah],
and-God [eloah] hedged [vayasekh] around-him?

**3:24** For before [lifnei] my-bread [lachmiy] my-sighing [anechatiy] comes,
and-poured-out [vayitteku] like-the-waters [ka-mayim] my-groanings [sha'agotay].

**3:25** For the-dread [pachad] I-dreaded [pachadetiiy] has-come-upon-me [yevoaniy],
and-that-which I-feared [yagoretiy] has-come [yavo] to-me.

**3:26** I-was-not at-ease [shalavtiy] and-I-was-not quiet [shaqattiy],
and-I-did-not rest [nachti], and-came [vayavo] turmoil [rogez]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — "Let perish the day":** The verb *yovad* (from *avad*) is a strong wish for annihilation — Iyyov does not merely regret being born; he wants the day itself erased from existence. The parallel "night" that announced conception shows he attacks both endpoints of his origin.

**v.8 — "Leviathan":** *Livyatan* here refers to the primordial chaos monster. Those who "curse the day" are mythological figures capable of unleashing cosmic disorder — Iyyov calls on them to unmake the day of his birth.

**v.23 — "hedged around him":** The verb *vayasekh* (to hedge/fence in) ironically echoes the Adversary's complaint in 1:10 that YHWH had "hedged" (*sakta*) Iyyov in with protection. Now the same fencing is experienced as imprisonment.

---
*— EMET*
